nodes.description: Public constant uint256 decimals = 8 defined in contract DC.
Public constant string symbol = "DC".
Public constant string name = "docoin".
Public uint256 _totalSupply = 10 ** 19, the fixed token supply.
Public address owner; set in the constructor to msg.sender.
Private mapping(address => uint256) balances tracking token balances.
Private nested mapping(address => mapping(address => uint256)) allowed for allowances.
Private mapping(address => bool) approvedInvestorList of whitelisted investors.
Private mapping(address => uint256) deposit recording ETH deposits per buyer.
Public uint256 totalTokenSold counter initialised to 0.
Constructor DC(): sets owner = msg.sender and credits balances[owner] with _totalSupply.
Constant function totalSupply() returning _totalSupply.
Constant function balanceOf(address _addr) returning balances[_addr].
Constant function isApprovedInvestor(address _addr) returning approvedInvestorList[_addr].
Constant function getDeposit(address _addr) returning deposit[_addr].
Public transfer(address _to, uint256 _amount) moving tokens from msg.sender to _to after a checked balance/overflow condition.
Public transferFrom(address _from, address _to, uint256 _amount) moving tokens using the caller's allowance.
Public approve(address _spender, uint256 _amount) writing allowed[msg.sender][_spender], requires zero-current-allowance or zero amount.
Constant function allowance(address _owner, address _spender) returning allowed[_owner][_spender].
Payable fallback function that unconditionally reverts, rejecting all plain ETH transfers.
Caller-controlled msg.sender used for ownership assignment, balance indexing and allowance indexing.
balances[msg.sender] -= _amount in transfer(); unchecked subtraction in Solidity 0.4.18, guarded only by the preceding balance check.
balances[_to] += _amount in transfer(); unchecked addition, guarded only by the balances[_to] + _amount > balances[_to] overflow test.
balances[_from] -= _amount in transferFrom(); unchecked subtraction relying on the balances[_from] >= _amount check.
allowed[_from][msg.sender] -= _amount in transferFrom(); unchecked allowance decrement.
balances[_to] += _amount in transferFrom(); unchecked addition without overflow protection.
allowed[msg.sender][_spender] = _amount in approve(); direct allowance overwrite for a caller-supplied spender.
owner = msg.sender in the constructor; privileged ownership assigned from an untrusted caller.
Parameter _to (address) of transfer(); used as the destination balance index.
Parameter _amount (uint256) of transfer(); the amount debited and credited.
Parameter _from (address) of transferFrom(); the debited balance owner.
Parameter _to (address) of transferFrom(); the credited recipient.
Parameter _amount (uint256) of transferFrom(); the amount moved and deducted from allowance.
Parameter _spender (address) of approve(); the address receiving the allowance.
Parameter _amount (uint256) of approve(); the allowance value written for the spender.

edges.reason: msg.sender indexes balances[...] in the decrement inside transfer().
msg.sender is the second key of allowed[_from][msg.sender] in transferFrom().
msg.sender is the allowance owner key written by approve().
Untrusted msg.sender becomes the contract owner in the constructor.
msg.sender is the only external input consumed by the constructor DC().
transfer() reads msg.sender for its balance lookup and Transfer event.
transferFrom() consumes msg.sender when checking and reducing the allowance.
approve() keys the allowance mapping on the caller msg.sender.
Parameter _amount is subtracted from balances[msg.sender] without overflow-safe math.
Parameter _amount is added to balances[_to] with only a manual overflow guard.
Parameter _to selects the balance entry credited in transfer().
Parameter _from selects the balance entry debited in transferFrom().
Parameter _amount is subtracted from balances[_from] with no overflow-safe arithmetic.
Parameter _amount is subtracted from the caller allowance without overflow-safe arithmetic.
Parameter _amount is added to balances[_to] in transferFrom() without overflow protection.
Parameter _to selects the balance entry credited in transferFrom().
Parameter _spender is the allowance key written in approve().
Parameter _amount is stored directly as an allowance value in approve().
transfer() executes the unchecked subtraction from the sender balance.
transfer() executes the unchecked addition to the recipient balance.
transferFrom() executes the unchecked subtraction from balances[_from].
transferFrom() executes the unchecked allowance decrement.
transferFrom() executes the unchecked addition to balances[_to].
approve() writes the caller-controlled allowance for _spender.
Constructor assigns ownership from the untrusted caller.
Constructor writes the owner state variable, establishing privileged access.
Constructor initialises balances[owner] with the total supply.
Constructor reads _totalSupply to mint the initial balance.
transfer() reads and writes the balances mapping.
transferFrom() reads and writes the balances mapping.
transferFrom() reads and writes the allowed mapping.
approve() reads and writes the allowed mapping.
balanceOf() returns balances[_addr], a read of the balances mapping.
allowance() returns allowed[_owner][_spender], a read of the allowed mapping.
totalSupply() returns the _totalSupply state variable.
getDeposit() returns deposit[_addr], a read of the deposit mapping.
isApprovedInvestor() returns approvedInvestorList[_addr], a read of the whitelist mapping.

normalization_plan.reason: The address _to parameter only exists to index the balances mapping inside transfer().
The uint256 _amount parameter is only meaningful inside transfer(), where it feeds the unsafe balance updates.
The address _from parameter only exists to select the debited balance inside transferFrom().
The address _to parameter only exists to select the credited balance inside transferFrom().
The uint256 _amount parameter is the operand of the unchecked allowance and balance subtractions in transferFrom().
The address _spender parameter only exists as the allowance key written inside approve().
The uint256 _amount parameter is the value assigned directly to the allowance slot in approve().
